nodes.summary: Assume equality of base types is decidable. Given a context $\Gamma$ (a list of simple types), a raw term $r$ and a simple type $A$, the type checker returns true exactly when type inference for $r$ in $\Gamma$ returns the type $A$, and false otherwise.
nodes.title: Type checking for raw STLC terms

nodes.summary: For a context $\Gamma$ of simple types, a checked term in $\Gamma$ is a pair $(A, t)$ of a simple type $A$ and an intrinsically typed term $t$ of type $A$ in $\Gamma$.
nodes.title: Checked terms

nodes.summary: A raw term $t$ is closed when its list of free indices at binder depth $0$ is empty.
nodes.title: Closed raw terms

nodes.summary: Let $\rho$ be a typed renaming from context $\Gamma$ to $\Delta$, let $\sigma$ be a typed renaming from $\Delta$ to $\Xi$, and let $r, s : \mathbb{N} \to \mathbb{N}$. If $\rho$ agrees with $r$ and $\sigma$ agrees with $s$, then the composite renaming that applies $\rho$ and then $\sigma$ agrees with $s \circ r$.
nodes.title: Agreement of renamings is preserved by composition

nodes.summary: Assume equality of base types is decidable. If a raw term $r$ has type $A$ in context $\Gamma$ under the declarative typing judgment, then elaborating $r$ in $\Gamma$ succeeds and returns the type $A$ together with some intrinsically typed term of type $A$ in $\Gamma$.
nodes.title: Completeness of elaboration

nodes.summary: Assume equality of base types is decidable. For every intrinsically typed term $t$ of type $A$ in context $\Gamma$, elaborating the erasure of $t$ in $\Gamma$ succeeds and returns exactly the pair $(A, t)$. In other words, erasure is a section of elaboration.
nodes.title: Elaboration inverts erasure

nodes.summary: Assume equality of base types is decidable. If elaborating a raw term $r$ in context $\Gamma$ succeeds with type $A$ and intrinsically typed term $t$, then the erasure of $t$ is exactly $r$.
nodes.title: Elaboration preserves the input syntax

nodes.summary: Assume equality of base types is decidable. If elaborating a raw term $r$ in context $\Gamma$ succeeds with type $A$ (and some intrinsically typed term of type $A$ in $\Gamma$), then $r$ has type $A$ in $\Gamma$ under the declarative typing judgment.
nodes.title: Soundness of elaboration

nodes.summary: Assume equality of base types is decidable. Elaboration in a context $\Gamma$ of simple types sends a raw term either to failure or to a checked term in $\Gamma$ (a simple type together with an intrinsically typed term of that type in $\Gamma$), by recursion on the raw term. A variable with de Bruijn index $n$ elaborates to the variable at position $n$ of $\Gamma$ (counting from $0$ at the front), with the type…
nodes.title: Elaboration of raw STLC terms

nodes.summary: For every intrinsically typed term $t$ of type $A$ in context $\Gamma$, the erasure of $t$ has type $A$ in $\Gamma$ under the declarative typing judgment for raw terms.
nodes.title: Erasure preserves typing

nodes.summary: For a fixed context $\Gamma$ and type $A$, erasure is injective on intrinsically typed terms of type $A$ in $\Gamma$: two such terms with the same erasure are equal.
nodes.title: Erasure is injective

nodes.summary: Let $\rho$ be a typed renaming from context $\Gamma$ to $\Delta$ and let $r : \mathbb{N} \to \mathbb{N}$ be a numerical renaming that agrees with $\rho$. Then for every intrinsically typed term $t$ of type $A$ in context $\Gamma$, the erasure of the renamed term $\rho(t)$ equals the raw renaming by $r$ (lifted at every binder) of the erasure of $t$.
nodes.title: Erasure commutes with renaming

nodes.summary: For every intrinsically typed term $t$ in context $\Gamma$ and every type $B$, the erasure of the weakening of $t$ to the context $\Gamma$ extended by $B$ equals the raw renaming by the successor map $n \mapsto n + 1$ (lifted at every binder) of the erasure of $t$. Thus every free index is incremented by one.
nodes.title: Erasure of a weakened term

nodes.summary: The erasure of an intrinsically typed term in a context $\Gamma$ is the raw term defined by recursion: a variable becomes the raw variable whose index is its position in $\Gamma$ (counting from $0$ at the front); an application of $f$ to $a$ becomes the raw application of the erasure of $f$ to the erasure of $a$; and a lambda with parameter type $B$ becomes the raw lambda annotated with $B$ whose body is the…
nodes.title: Erasure of intrinsically typed terms

nodes.summary: For a binder depth $d$ and a raw term $t$, the free indices of $t$ at depth $d$ form a list defined by recursion on $t$: a variable with index $n$ contributes $[n - d]$ if $d \le n$ and the empty list otherwise; an application contributes the free indices of the function followed by those of the argument, both at depth $d$; and a lambda abstraction contributes the free indices of its body at depth $d + 1$.
nodes.title: Free indices of a raw term

nodes.summary: For a context $\Gamma$ (a list of simple types), a raw term $t$ and a type $A$, the judgment $\Gamma \vdash t : A$ is the least relation closed under three rules. A variable with de Bruijn index $n$ has type $A$ in $\Gamma$ whenever looking up $n$ in $\Gamma$ succeeds with the type $A$ and some intrinsic variable of type $A$. If $\Gamma \vdash f : A \Rightarrow B$ and $\Gamma \vdash a : A$, then the application…
nodes.title: Declarative typing of raw terms

nodes.summary: Assume equality of base types is decidable. For every context $\Gamma$, raw term $t$ and type $A$, the declarative typing judgment $\Gamma \vdash t : A$ holds if and only if there is an intrinsically typed term $u$ of type $A$ in context $\Gamma$ such that elaborating $t$ in $\Gamma$ succeeds and returns the type $A$ together with $u$.
nodes.title: Declarative typing agrees with elaboration

nodes.summary: The list of de Bruijn indices of a raw term, read from left to right with repetitions: a variable with index $n$ gives $[n]$, an application gives the indices of the function followed by those of the argument, and a lambda abstraction gives the indices of its body, unshifted.
nodes.title: Indices occurring in a raw term

nodes.summary: Assume equality of base types is decidable. For every context $\Gamma$, raw term $t$ and type $A$, type inference for $t$ in $\Gamma$ returns $A$ if and only if the declarative typing judgment $\Gamma \vdash t : A$ holds.
nodes.title: Type inference is sound and complete

nodes.summary: Assume equality of base types is decidable. Given a context $\Gamma$ and a raw term $t$, type inference elaborates $t$ in $\Gamma$; if elaboration succeeds, it returns the type component of the result and forgets the intrinsically typed term, and if elaboration fails, inference fails.
nodes.title: Type inference for raw terms

nodes.summary: For maps $\rho, \sigma : \mathbb{N} \to \mathbb{N}$, the lift of $\sigma \circ \rho$ through one binder equals the lift of $\sigma$ composed after the lift of $\rho$.
nodes.title: Lifting commutes with composition of numerical renamings

nodes.summary: Given a renaming $\rho : \mathbb{N} \to \mathbb{N}$ of de Bruijn indices, its lift through one binder is the map $\mathbb{N} \to \mathbb{N}$ sending $0$ to $0$ and $n + 1$ to $\rho(n) + 1$.
nodes.title: Lifting a numerical renaming

nodes.summary: Let $\rho$ be a typed renaming from context $\Gamma$ to $\Delta$ and let $r : \mathbb{N} \to \mathbb{N}$ be a numerical renaming that agrees with $\rho$. Then for every type $A$, the lift of $\rho$ under a binder of type $A$ agrees with the lift of $r$ through one binder.
nodes.title: Agreement of renamings is preserved by lifting

nodes.summary: For every context $\Gamma$ and natural number $n$, if looking up the de Bruijn index $n$ in $\Gamma$ succeeds with a type $A$ and an intrinsic variable $x$ of type $A$ in $\Gamma$, then the de Bruijn index of $x$ is $n$.
nodes.title: Lookup returns a variable with the queried index

nodes.summary: For every context $\Gamma$, type $A$ and intrinsic variable $x$ of type $A$ in $\Gamma$, looking up the de Bruijn index of $x$ in $\Gamma$ succeeds and returns the type $A$ together with $x$.
nodes.title: Lookup recovers an intrinsic variable from its index

nodes.summary: Given a context $\Gamma$, a list of types, and a natural number $n$, looking up the de Bruijn index $n$ in $\Gamma$ either fails or returns a type $A$ together with an intrinsic variable of type $A$ in $\Gamma$. It is defined by recursion: lookup fails in the empty context; index $0$ in the context $A :: \Gamma$, obtained by adding $A$ at the front of $\Gamma$, returns $A$ with the zero variable; and index $n + 1$…
nodes.title: Variable lookup

nodes.summary: Assume equality of base types is decidable. For every intrinsically typed term $t$ of type $A$ in context $\Gamma$, raw normalization of the erasure of $t$ in $\Gamma$ succeeds and returns the type $A$ together with the erasure of the normal form of $t$ computed by normalization by evaluation.
nodes.title: Raw normalization of an erased term

nodes.summary: Assume equality of base types is decidable. For every context $\Gamma$ and raw term $t$, if raw normalization of $t$ in $\Gamma$ succeeds with a type $A$ and a raw term $t'$, then the declarative typing judgment $\Gamma \vdash t' : A$ holds.
nodes.title: Raw normalization produces well-typed terms

nodes.summary: Assume equality of base types is decidable. For every context $\Gamma$ and raw term $t$, if raw normalization of $t$ in $\Gamma$ succeeds with a type $A$ and a raw term $t'$, then raw normalization of $t'$ in $\Gamma$ succeeds with the same type $A$ and the same term $t'$.
nodes.title: Raw normalization is idempotent

nodes.summary: Let the base types have decidable equality, let $\Gamma$ be a context of simple types and let $r$ be a raw term. If normalizing $r$ in $\Gamma$ succeeds and returns a type $A$ together with a raw term, then type inference for $r$ in $\Gamma$ returns $A$.
nodes.title: Raw normalization reports the inferred type

nodes.summary: Let the base types have decidable equality. Given a context $\Gamma$ of simple types and a raw term $r$, raw normalization elaborates $r$ in $\Gamma$. If elaboration fails, raw normalization fails. If elaboration returns a type $A$ and an intrinsically typed term $t$ of type $A$, raw normalization returns $A$ together with the erasure to a raw term of the normal form of $t$ computed by normalization by evaluation.
nodes.title: Normalization of raw terms

nodes.summary: Raw terms are extrinsic de Bruijn syntax over a given type of base types: a raw term is either a variable given by a natural-number index $n$, an application $f\,a$ of two raw terms $f$ and $a$, or a lambda abstraction $\lambda A.\,t$ consisting of a simple type $A$ over the base types (the parameter type) and a raw term $t$ (the body). Variables and applications carry no type information.
nodes.title: Raw lambda terms

nodes.summary: A typed renaming $\rho$ from context $\Gamma$ to context $\Delta$ agrees with a map $r : \mathbb{N} \to \mathbb{N}$ when, for every type $A$ and every variable $x$ of type $A$ in $\Gamma$, the de Bruijn index of $\rho(x)$ equals $r$ applied to the de Bruijn index of $x$.
nodes.title: Agreement of a typed and a numerical renaming

nodes.summary: For all maps $\rho, \sigma : \mathbb{N} \to \mathbb{N}$ and every raw term $t$, renaming $t$ by $\rho$ and then renaming the result by $\sigma$ gives the same raw term as renaming $t$ by the composite $\sigma \circ \rho$.
nodes.title: Composition of renamings of raw terms

nodes.summary: Let $\rho$ be a type-preserving renaming of variables from context $\Gamma$ to context $\Delta$, and let $r, s : \mathbb{N} \to \mathbb{N}$ both agree with $\rho$: for every variable $x$ of $\Gamma$, the de Bruijn index of $\rho(x)$ is the image of the index of $x$ under $r$, and also under $s$. Then for every intrinsically typed term $t$ of type $A$ in context $\Gamma$, renaming the erasure of $t$ by $r$ and…
nodes.title: Agreeing numerical renamings coincide on erased terms

nodes.summary: Given a map $\rho : \mathbb{N} \to \mathbb{N}$ on de Bruijn indices, renaming a raw term by $\rho$ replaces each variable $n$ by $\rho(n)$, renames both parts of an application by $\rho$, and renames the body of a lambda abstraction, keeping its parameter type, by the lifted map $\rho'$ given by $\rho'(0) = 0$ and $\rho'(n + 1) = \rho(n) + 1$.
nodes.title: Renaming of raw terms

nodes.summary: For natural numbers $k$ (the amount) and $c$ (the cutoff, $0$ by default), shifting a raw term by $k$ at cutoff $c$ replaces a variable index $n$ by $n + k$ if $c \le n$ and leaves it unchanged otherwise, shifts both sides of an application by $k$ at cutoff $c$, and sends $\lambda A.\,t$ to $\lambda A.\,t'$, where $t'$ is $t$ shifted by $k$ at cutoff $c + 1$.
nodes.title: Shifting raw terms

nodes.summary: For every map $\rho : \mathbb{N} \to \mathbb{N}$ and every raw term $t$, the renaming of $t$ by $\rho$ has the same number of syntax nodes as $t$.
nodes.title: Renaming preserves the size of a raw term

nodes.summary: For all natural numbers $k$ and $c$ and every raw term $t$, shifting $t$ by $k$ at cutoff $c$ (adding $k$ to each variable index that is at least the cutoff, which grows by one under each binder) gives a raw term with the same number of syntax nodes as $t$.
nodes.title: Shifting preserves the size of a raw term

nodes.summary: Writing $|t|$ for the size of a raw term $t$, the size counts the syntax nodes of $t$: a variable has size $1$, an application $f\,a$ has size $|f| + |a| + 1$, and a lambda abstraction $\lambda A.\,t$ has size $|t| + 1$, so the type annotation $A$ is not counted.
nodes.title: Size of a raw term

nodes.summary: For a context $\Gamma$ and a type $A$, a well-typed de Bruijn variable of type $A$ in $\Gamma$ is sent to its natural-number index, forgetting its type: the variable for the first entry of the context has index $0$, and the successor of a variable $x$ has the index of $x$ plus $1$.
nodes.title: Index of a typed variable

nodes.summary: Let $\Gamma$ be a context of simple types and $r$ a raw term. If $r$ has type $A$ in $\Gamma$ and $r$ has type $B$ in $\Gamma$ under the declarative typing judgment for raw terms, then $A = B$.
nodes.title: Uniqueness of types for raw terms

can_prove.label: ready to prove
can_prove.meaning: Statement is in Lean and nothing it needs is blocked, so the proof can start.

can_state.label: ready to state
can_state.meaning: Everything its statement uses is in Lean, so the statement can be written in Lean.

conditional.label: conditionally proved
conditional.meaning: Proof compiles, but rests on an open statement without a recorded Lean proof.

fully_proved.label: fully proved
fully_proved.meaning: Proved, and every prerequisite is fully proved too.

inventory_checked.label: inventory checked
inventory_checked.meaning: Module inventory checked in full; it records inspection, not a mathematical proof.

inventory_pending.label: inventory pending
inventory_pending.meaning: Module inventory not yet checked in full; it records inspection, not a mathematical proof.

not_ready.label: not ready
not_ready.meaning: Needs more blueprint work before it can be attempted.

proved.label: proved
proved.meaning: Proof compiles, but something it rests on is not finished.

stated.label: statement formalized
stated.meaning: Statement is in Lean; the proof is not.
